_comment: CORS routers Aeos can put in front of blocked API hosts. Per-filter status comes from live LinkLens category checks; 'unknown' means the filter timed out or errored during the check and must not be treated as a pass. Auto-selection only picks entries with autoSelect:true and status 'unblocked' for the active filter.

routers.name: Aeos Router
routers.note: Self-hosted Supabase edge function. First choice: no signup, no key, and the fastest of the set. The target must be percent-encoded -- passed verbatim, the upstream's own query string is absorbed by the outer ?url=. GoGuardian and LanSchool are marked unblocked from direct testing rather than a category lookup.

routers.name: cors.lol
routers.note: No signup, no key. Drop-in replacement for a direct request.

routers.name: Corsfix
setupSteps: Open the Corsfix sign-up page and create an account. Never use a school or work email for this.
Once you are in the dashboard, copy your API key.
Paste the key below. Aeos stores it on this device only and sends it as the x-corsfix-key header.

routers.name: CORS.SH
setupSteps: Open the CORS.SH console and sign in. Never use a school or work email for this.
Create a new project. Set the allowed origin to the URL shown below and leave allowed targets blank.
Copy the LIVE key (it starts with live_) and paste it below. Aeos sends it as the x-cors-api-key header.

routers.name: WhateverOrigin
routers.note: No signup, but it answers with a JSON envelope ({"contents":...}) instead of the upstream body, so it is not a drop-in replacement and is offered as a manual choice only.

retired.name: corsproxy.io
retired.reason: No longer functional, and blocked by most filters. Existing saved values are cleared on load.

retired.name: allorigins
retired.reason: Unverified host that was never part of the tested set.
